preliminary_validation.qualified_as: Earlier revision only; final additional-data role case and Changed diagnostic were rebuilt and rerun on all three platforms.

guarantees: Sealed immutable result only after all query phases complete, retaining the exact originally opened native object.
Independent basic/storage/link/channel/attribute/security query states and coverage survive. No unsupported/denied/unknown observation becomes empty or absent.
Every listed attribute receives an indexed value observation; all six explicitly scoped security parts are attempted. No privilege elevation or weaker-query fallback.
Exact feature namespaces and native units; malformed catalog envelopes, duplicates, mismatched keys and resource violations prevent completed output.
Native query-buffer budgets remain separate from cumulative retained identifier/value/link payload limits.
Cooperative 256-step advances, injected clock/time slices, resumable cancellation, completed-query progress across yields, exception poisoning and worker-side resource release.
Identity continuity and per-payload owner comparisons are explicit; Same never asserts stable content or a frozen inventory.
validation_notes: 105-file manifest includes test host and both native adapters. Remote extraction verified every source hash; all final local hashes still match. Documentation-only edits do not alter tested code.

Final normal increments on every platform compiled inventory implementation and domain/native fixtures, rebuilt core library and linked both executables (six steps). Mac comparable earlier six-step builds took 3.471/3.366 s; final 3.729 s. Linux/Windows final six-step builds took 5.663/9.782 s. Compiled units, links, timestamps, output hashes and all 23 new RUN markers checked.

Direct sanitizers compiled 30 units without cached objects: Mac/Linux/Windows final 49.845/120.513/55.657 s versus preliminary same-scope 49.694/117.740/53.824 s. All final 49 cases passed; strict warnings remained errors, supported sanitizer options halted on diagnostics. No reported diagnostics.

Final review separated native wire buffers from retained identifier accounting, preserved additional-data attribute roles/bytes, and used Changed/MetadataChanged for a mismatched attribute identifier. Revised source was rebuilt and rerun, never accepted from earlier binaries.

Native tests used exclusively created task scratch directories. Name replacement via rename, removal, cancellation/resume and result retirement tested on all three OSes. Windows delete-pending namespace lifetime was respected; no immediate POSIX name reuse assumption.

Preliminary and final diagnostic executables hashed and zero-owner checks passed before removal. Final full scratch-root audits empty. Current verified normal builds remain; no GUI launched or production mutation added.
Mac TMPDIR explicitly below mounted S8T. Windows source/build/cache/test/temp outputs on V:. Linux used its local task root and TMPDIR.

WP-01 first checklist item (strict core/platform targets, injected filesystem/time, identities, fakes, explicit ownership) is complete. Remaining WP-01 items and acceptance remain open; WP-02..08 not started.
limitations: Completion means collection phases finished, not complete feature coverage, a snapshot, frozen namespace or preservation feasibility.

No main-data/named-stream content API used. Attribute values are explicitly read and can contain additional file data/security markings. Native provider guards still apply; no universal no-hydration guarantee or hydration consent supplied.

Native methods may contain multiple blocking syscalls. Comparisons, allocations and retirement can overrun a cooperative time slice. No scheduler, UI publication protocol or large-view/disk-backed inventory store implemented here.
Retained payload/count budgets are not a process-memory quota and do not bound diagnostic strings or an adapter temporary allocation; a query reply can coexist with staging.

Initial selection acquisition, remaining native inventory categories, operation-specific capabilities, collision/equivalence rules and worker/UI/large-view integration remain. Mutations, preservation consent and recovery still require later packages.
